2026 SEMA Show • Toyota Puts Snow Tracks on Five SUVs and Trucks, Unloads Them at SEMA 2026 as the Snowhunter Bunch
All-New Toyota Century Coupe Luxury Grand Tourer Gets Rendered in All-Black Production Guise Attire
9 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
Since Toyota Motor Corporation is the world’s best-selling automaker and also the most valuable representative of the automotive industry, it can allow itself to dream big in all sorts of directions.
TMC’s lofty targets for electric fuel cell models are well known, along with the fact that they never materialized, for example. But they have other ideas, too, like Gazoo Racing becoming an independent brand all over again and establishing itself with the upcoming GR GT hybrid V8 sports car. But that’s not all, of course.
Worldwide, the most renowned TMC brands are the namesake Toyota and the premium Lexus division, but a little more than a year ago Toyota debuted its former Century nameplate as a standalone brand at the 2025 Japan Mobility Show, taking a page out of Hyundai and Genesis’ playbook in the process.
Initially and for decades on end, the Toyota Century was the most luxurious car ever created in Japan – debuting in sedan form in 1967 and mostly reserved for domestic sales to government officials and major business elites. It mostly remained the same for decades – until in 2023, when it also gained an SUV sibling.
Now, the shift is even more pronounced because the Century has become a stand-alone brand that will reign on top of all TMC offerings on par with the likes of Rolls-Royce or Bentley. They announced the split with a slightly high-riding Century grand tourer coupe concept that looked ready to take on the Bentley Continental GT or the Rolls-Royce Spectre at a moment’s notice.
Of course, these things take time to develop, and the last time we heard anything about Century it was in October 2026 when Toyota looked to make its new Century brand a global asset, as the plug-in hybrid V6-powered Century SUV has expanded to China and to other countries in Asia and the Middle East in very small volumes.
Now, the Century brand has also caught the attention of a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and took another look at the striking Century high-riding coupe concept introduced last year.
More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on making the dreams of Toyota entirely possible with a production version of the Century grand tourer. It’s dressed in all-black attire now and keeps most of the prototype’s design traits while also looking ready for series production – and it even gains a set of deeply concave black alloy wheels courtesy of the aftermarket realm in the CGI process.
Also, the pixel master doesn’t let it alone across the plains of Imagination Land – they showcase it back-to-back with the competition, a Bentley Continental GT feeling a bit blue about itself or green with envy, but also compared to the real world’s concept car. So, what do you think? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
